        "statement": "In this chapter, the term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes: (I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including how the disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum, for preschool children (as appropriate) participation in appropriate activities, and for children taking alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, benchmarks or short-term objectives; (II) a statement of measurable annual goals (including academic and functional goals) designed to meet disability-related needs enabling involvement/progress in the general education curriculum and meet each other educational need resulting from the disability; (III) a description of how progress toward meeting annual goals will be measured and when periodic progress reports will be provided; (IV) a statement of special education, related services, and supplementary aids and services (based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable) and program modifications or supports for school personnel to advance toward annual goals, be involved/progress in general curriculum, participate in extracurricular/nonacademic activities, and be educated/participate with disabled and nondisabled children; (V) an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in regular class and activities; (VI)(aa) a statement of necessary individual appropriate accommodations to measure academic achievement and functional performance on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A), and (bb) if the IEP Team determines an alternate assessment is to be taken, a statement of why the child cannot participate in regular assessment and why the selected alternate assessment is appropriate; (VII) projected start dates and anticipated frequency, location, and duration of services and modifications; and (VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP in effect when the child is 16 (updated annually), appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based on age-appropriate transition assessments, needed transition services (including courses of study), and beginning not later than 1 year before reaching majority age under State law, a statement that the child was informed of rights transferring on reaching majority age under section 1415(m).",
